title: Knowledge check: Authentication and Authorization Middleware

questions.prompt: In Authentication and Authorization Middleware, which statement best describes Checking identity?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.

Connect this syllabus point to Authentication and Authorization Middleware: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Authorization checks what the verified identity may do. Enforce permissions and resource ownership in the server for every protected operation; hiding a button is not access control.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Authentication and Authorization Middleware?
options: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.
questions.explanation: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.

questions.prompt: A change related to Authentication and Authorization Middleware appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
